# Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies

# Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Hyperliquid ALO write priority (official docs): ALO orders are processed FIFO as transactions, with similar end-to-end latency as cancels, and all cancels are prioritized before all immediately executable orders. An optional ALO priority fee is charged from undelegated staking balance as a fraction of resting notional and is deducted at placement regardless of whether the order fills; on the timescale of 400ms it sorts only the tail of the queue at each level, made up of orders placed within the past 400ms. IOC priority has an effect of approximately 45 ms reduction in end-to-end latency per 1 bp of priority fee, linear from 0-8bps. A taker-signal strategy converted to ALO is handled in the cancel-speed lane, but paying for queue position costs money even when the order never fills (inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/priority-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide, https://multicoin.capital/2026/02/17/adverse-selection-rules-everything-around-me/
- [statement] Hyperliquid documents queue priority for ALO orders. On the timescale of 400ms, the tail of the queue at each level, made up of orders placed within the past 400ms, is sorted by priority rate. The rate is charged from undelegated staking balance as a fraction of resting notional in the case of ALO, and the fees are deducted at time of placing the order regardless of whether the order fills. ALO orders are processed FIFO as transactions with similar end-to-end latency as cancels. A third-party guide dates the ALO priority fee to July 2026; the official page read here carries no date for it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/priority-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide

## How it works

- [statement] Albers et al. conclude it is challenging to overcome the taker fee with taker strategies even when the signal has a robust pre-fee edge, and that maker strategies, despite not paying taker fees, do not offer an easy way around that because of queue position, fill probability and price drift. Their abstract says viable maker strategies often need to be contrarian to the prevailing order-book imbalance. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1
- [statement] A Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 1, 2026 shows a Hyperliquid close order submitted as a BUY LIMIT_MAKER on HYPE-USD rejected with 'Reduce only order would increase position'; this is a reduce-only reject, not a post-only cross reject, and the root cause was not established in the thread. (low confidence) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8269
- [statement] Albers et al. build a reversal model that predicts when the imbalance falsely signals the next move. Balanced-inventory maker trading gated by the logistic model at threshold 0.24 had 327 round trips per day and an average return of 0.71 bp per round trip, against an average loss of 0.44 bp (net of rebates) for the naive strategy; the Sharpe ratio improves from -109 to 11.97. The returns include a maker rebate on each leg of the roundtrip. The authors say the strategy is slightly profitable with min-sized orders and assuming low fees, albeit those profits are likely not scalable, and that it demonstrates a proof-of-concept. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Hyperliquid ALO rejections are routine in live bots. A Hyperliquid TWAP bot's mainnet logs for 2026-08-20..23 show 531 ALO rejections, all 'Post only order would have immediately matched', next to 2,305 resting ALOs. In another bot, when both ALO attempts are rejected the function returns before registering the IOC for the remainder, so the entry is abandoned silently, with no IOC and no fill line. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/howlrs/hype-trigger-twap/pull/53 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/rcerucci/hl-jev/issues/42, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/error-responses

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] On a Lighter Standard account regular perpetual orders pay 0 maker and 0 taker fee, so converting a taker entry to post-only saves no fee; the only gain is the spread not crossed (plus slippage on size). Plus accounts pay 0.5bps and Premium/Advanced accounts pay 0.0040% maker / 0.0280% taker at zero staked LIT, where the maker discount is real. This is an inference from the Lighter fee tables. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills: between deciding to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine the order can still get filled, and those fills are the worst because the market is about to run through the quote. Applied to Lighter Standard's 300ms cancel latency, this is an inference, not a measurement on Lighter. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Lighter fee schedule for conversion economics: Standard accounts pay 0 maker and 0 taker on regular perpetual and spot orders (1 bp on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ); Plus accounts pay 0.5bps; Premium/Advanced accounts pay 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker at zero staked LIT, with a 30% discount at 500,000 staked LIT (0.0028% maker, 0.0196% taker). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] Official fee schedules: Paradex Retail pays 0% maker and taker; Paradex Pro pays a flat 0.005% (0.5 bps) maker against a taker fee of 0.045% at the base tier, floored at 1.75 bps after discounts; Hyperliquid tier 0 pays 0.015% maker against 0.045% taker. A maker fee advantage therefore exists on paid tiers but not on the zero-fee Retail route. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees, https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide
- [statement] Paradex keeps two books. The UI and interactive-token (Retail) orders see RPI liquidity, which only Retail takers can match, which must be post-only and which has the lowest priority at its price. The API book excludes RPI, so a Pro (default API) post-only order rests in a book without RPI quotes. OpenChainBench reports that the two books can diverge on thin pairs (SOL on 2026-09-22: 0.03 % spread on the interactive book against 1.4 % on the API book; a single-day vendor figure). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://openchainbench.com/benchmarks/perp-fees
- [statement] Latency must be in the simulator. Albers et al. say their imbalance-strategy comparison ignores latency, 'potentially leading to an overstatement of results'. a vendor article says simulators that seed queue position at decision time overestimate queue priority by the volume that arrives during the latency window. For these venues the inputs follow the docs (inference): Lighter Standard 0 ms maker latency and 300 ms cancel/modify and taker latency; Paradex Retail 300ms for submission and cancellation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/, https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/Market%20Making%20with%20Alpha%20-%20Order%20Book%20Imbalance.html, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Published maker-with-signal results are rebate-dependent. The hftbacktest tutorial's order-book-imbalance market maker (Binance BTCUSDT) bases its backtests on a 0.005% rebate; its return per trade drops from 0.0139% to 0.0086% including the 0.005% rebates in February 2025 after the power_prob_queue_model parameter was changed from 2 to 3 to reflect a more challenging fill in the queue. The author says this highlights the importance of rebates. Albers et al.'s gated rows also include a maker rebate on each leg of the roundtrip. (medium confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/Market%20Making%20with%20Alpha%20-%20Order%20Book%20Imbalance.html · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Re-pegging by amend resets queue priority. A vendor article states that on virtually every crypto venue an amend is a cancel/replace that returns a new order ID at the back of the queue, so a quoting engine that re-pegs every 500ms is perpetually re-entering at the back. NautilusTrader's docs say Hyperliquid modifies orders by cancel-replace: the modify action cancels the original order (old oid) and opens a replacement with a new oid. Moallemi and Yuan find that adverse selection costs increase with queue position. A chase-style conversion loop therefore trades fill rate against priority. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/integrations/hyperliquid/, https://moallemi.com/ciamac/papers/queue-value-2016.pdf
- [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills. A vendor article says fills that arrive between the decision to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine are the worst fills, because the market was about to run through the quote, and a simulator without cancel latency deletes exactly those fills. Lighter Standard (300 ms cancel/modify) and Paradex Retail (300ms cancellation speed bump) both impose that window by design; Lighter Premium/Advanced and Paradex Pro do not. Inference: the effect applies on these venues but has not been measured on them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Conversion pays only if the fee gap plus the spread saved beats adverse drift and missed trades, so the fee tier decides. Lighter Standard accounts pay 0 maker and 0 taker on regular perpetual orders. Lighter Premium/Advanced at zero staked LIT pays 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker. Hyperliquid's base perpetual tier pays 0.015% maker and 0.045% taker. Against that, Daru measured negative 10-second pre-fee entry markouts for a touch quoter (-0.39 to -0.84 bp across Bybit, Binance USD-M and Hyperliquid), and its Bybit depth panel finds no level profitable per quoting opportunity below a 0.328 bp rebate. This is an inference from fee tables and third-party markouts, not a measurement on these venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees, https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] In the hl-jev bot the ALO rests and an IOC after 8 s takes the remainder. Its first logged entry fill (buy 0.11 @ 121.73) had fill_role: taker, so the IOC fallback, not the resting ALO, supplied that fill. In practice a converted strategy becomes a maker-first, taker-fallback hybrid, and its realised fee and slippage mix depends on the timeout. (low confidence) — https://github.com/rcerucci/hl-jev/issues/42
- [statement] Re-pegging a post-only order is a cost lever, not free maintenance. A vendor article says a price amend is a cancel/replace on virtually every crypto venue that returns a new order ID at the back of the queue, so a quoter that re-pegs every 500ms is perpetually re-entering at the back. In Daru's simulation, loosening the re-quote condition removes at least 28.5% of the measured adverse selection on Bybit and 32.7% on Hyperliquid (a floor, not a point estimate), so frequent re-posting adds adverse selection. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/DaruFinance/crypto-adverse-selection, https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills. Between the decision to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine the order can still get filled, and the vendor article says those fills are the worst because the market was about to run through the quote. Albers et al. state that ignoring latency can overstate their strategy results. Applied to Lighter Standard's 300ms cancel latency or Paradex Retail's 300ms cancellation speed bump, this is an inference, not a measurement on those venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Maker fills coincide with adverse price moves. DeLise proves and measures a negative drift of a limit order fill (10 Year US Treasury Bond futures). Albers et al. document, in a live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual, a negative correlation between a maker order's fill probability and its subsequent return, because an order at the top of the queue fills with probability 1 when the next price move is against it. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Lighter latency asymmetry: Standard accounts have taker latency 300ms, maker latency 0ms and cancel/modify latency 300ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have no added latency on cancels or Post Only placements and 140 ms taker latency. A maker-converted strategy on a Standard account can post instantly but cannot pull a stale quote for 300ms. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] Backtests of a maker-converted strategy that assume a fill whenever price touches the limit overstate results. A worked example by a market-data vendor (plain symmetric maker, one month BTCUSDT perpetual) moves from +$9,600 under touch-fill to -$700 under a calibrated queue-depletion model, with a live shadow run at -$1,150; Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang found hypothetical first-passage executions are very poor proxies for actual limit-order executions. The vendor figures are a constructed illustration of a market maker, not a signal-taker conversion. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf
- [statement] Lighter latency by account type: Standard and Plus accounts have taker latency 300 ms, maker latency 0 ms and cancel/modify latency 300 ms; Premium/Advanced accounts have no added latency on cancels or Post Only placements and 140 ms taker latency. On Standard, a post-only entry has 0 ms latency against 300 ms for taker orders, but a stale quote cannot be pulled for 300 ms. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] Touch-fill backtests overstate maker and maker-converted results. Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang find hypothetical limit-order executions built from first-passage times or transaction data are very poor proxies for actual limit-order executions. DeLise shows that backtest simulations using synthetic data and random-fill assumptions appear to be profitable but in reality fail to produce a profit. Freqtrade's backtester documents that all orders are filled at the requested price as long as the price is within the candle's high/low range. A vendor worked example on one BTCUSDT perpetual month moves from +$9,600 (touch on 1m bars) to -$700 (calibrated queue-depletion) against -$1,150 in a live shadow run. (high confidence) — https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1, https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/backtesting/, https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/
- [statement] Bar-based backtests cannot order events inside a bar. Claeys measured that 18.47% of 2,064,460 one-minute E-mini NASDAQ-100 bars (from 2020 through 2025) are ambiguous for a 10-point stop and 10-point target scalp, with a best-case to worst-case gap of 3,695 NQ points ($73,900) per 1,000 trades, and five platforms resolve the ambiguity differently. Freqtrade's docs say backtesting can never be perfect and 'will always be biased in one way or the other'. A converted entry whose limit, stop and target sit in one bar has the same ambiguity (futures evidence, not perps). (medium confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm?abstractid=6240638&mirid=1&type=2 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/backtesting/
- [statement] Signal type decides whether post-only conversion can work. Albers et al. say viable maker strategies often require a contrarian approach, counter-trading the prevailing order book imbalance. Moallemi and Yuan find that adverse selection costs increase with queue position, and DeLise finds that limit order fills are caused by and coincide with adverse price movements. Inference: continuation or momentum entries convert poorly, fade or mean-reversion entries convert better. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://moallemi.com/ciamac/papers/queue-value-2016.pdf, https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1
- [statement] Fill probability falls steeply as the order moves away from the touch, while per-fill drift improves only modestly. Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang find execution times very sensitive to limit price. On a separate sample of 300 Bybit coin-days (buy side only), Daru's net per fill improves from -0.72 bp at the touch to -0.33 bp at the fifth level, but fills far less often, at 12% of the touch's rate. Inference: for a signal with a short half-life, a deeper post-only entry mostly turns into a missed trade. (medium confidence) — https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] Hyperliquid's Chase order is a Post Only (ALO) limit order that re-prices to track the best bid or ask. It rests one tick above the best bid (buys) or one tick below the best ask (sells), or at the best bid/ask when the spread is a single tick. It runs in the browser tab where it was created, up to 5 can be active, and it terminates on a rejection (for example below minimum notional or insufficient margin), when the limit order it placed is modified, when the tab is closed or refreshed, when the active address is switched, or when the same address is connected in another browser. The exchange endpoint documents limit orders (tif Alo, Ioc or Gtc) and trigger orders, so an API bot should expect to run its own cancel/replace loop (inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/order-types · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/support/faq/trade-outcome-looks-incorrect/why-was-my-chase-order-canceled, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint
- [statement] Hyperliquid rate limits for cancel/replace loops: the address-based limit allows 1 request per 1 USDC traded cumulatively since address inception, with an initial buffer of 10000 requests; when rate limited, an address is allowed one request every 10 seconds; cancels have cumulative limit min(limit + 100000, limit * 2); the default open order limit is 1000 plus one additional order for every 5M USDC of volume, capped at a total of 5000 open orders. A fresh account that re-pegs aggressively can burn its buffer quickly (inference) but keeps extra cancel headroom. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/rate-limits-and-user-limits · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide
- [statement] Daru's makercex command-line tool (makercex measure --snapshots book.parquet --trades tape.parquet --horizon 10s) measures the entry markout of a passive quote against true-aggressor-signed tape, with cluster-robust intervals that abstain when the panel cannot support one. It can score your own book and tape, but the study documents it as a one-leg measurement with no exit, inventory, fee or rebate. (low confidence) — https://github.com/DaruFinance/crypto-adverse-selection · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] Hyperliquid modify race: modifying a resting ALO order to a price that would cross cancels the original and then rejects the replacement as post-only, leaving no order. NautilusTrader's docs say an executable ALO or GTC replacement can cancel the original limit order before Hyperliquid rejects the replacement, and 'A modify rejection does not prove that the original order is still open.' A MetaMask issue reports a testnet run where a real ALO buy edited across the spread returned 'Error placing new order during modify: Post only order would have immediately matched, bbo was 2344.8@2345.2.' and orderStatus then reported the original order canceled. Query order status after any rejected modify before resubmitting. (medium confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/integrations/hyperliquid/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/metamask/metamask-mobile/issues/38352
- [statement] Fills on a resting limit order are not a random sample of the market. DeLise proves a negative drift for limit-order fills and confirms it on 10 Year US Treasury Bond futures. In a one-week live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual (232,897 minimum-sized maker orders, of which 127,051 filled), Albers et al. find that fill probability and post-fill return are negatively correlated, with a negative expected return of approximately -0.8 bp (-0.3 bp net of rebate). In Lalor and Swishchuk's table for a basic posting strategy on four CME futures (single April 2024 days), for example ES had 767 adverse fills of 941. A post-only entry therefore tends to fill when the market is moving through it. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2409.12721

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Post-only means cancel-on-cross, not slide-to-touch, on all three venues. Lighter cancels a Post-Only limit order if crossing orders exist at placement. Paradex cancels a post-only order that would immediately match. Hyperliquid's API says an ALO order will be canceled instead of immediately matching and lists the error 'Post only order would have immediately matched, bbo was {bbo}.' A converted strategy therefore gets a cancelled order, not a fill, whenever its limit price is marketable on arrival, and must reprice or skip. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/order-types-and-matching · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/orders/order-instructions, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/error-responses
- [statement] The practical protocol is a bracket, not a point estimate. The vendor article says a maker strategy is deployable only if it survives at the conservative edge of the bracket of fill rules. hftbacktest's RiskAverseQueueModel is its most conservative queue model. Nautilus offers a queue_position option for displayed-queue tracking and warns that a print proves that liquidity existed momentarily, not that it stayed available. Moallemi and Yuan, as cited by the vendor, find that for large-tick instruments the value of a front-of-queue position versus back-of-queue is comparable to the half-spread. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/py-v2.1.0/order_fill.html, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/backtesting/fill-prices-and-matching/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Re-pegging a post-only order every few hundred milliseconds re-enters at the back of the queue each time, so its realistic fill profile is mostly adverse selection; queue position is the price of re-quoting. A chase-style convert-to-maker loop for a taker signal therefore trades fill rate against priority. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] A Hummingbot issue opened on Dec 20, 2023 logs a Hyperliquid reject, 'Only post-only orders allowed immediately after a network upgrade', after a 500 code server disconnect; a converted strategy that needs taker fallback has no taker path during such windows. Single bug report, from 2023. (low confidence) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/6730
- [statement] Same-signal comparison from one live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual (February 12 to 19, 2024, 232,897 minimum-sized maker orders; under its most favorable tier the taker fee is 1.5 bp and the maker fee is -0.5 bp, a rebate). An order-book-imbalance taker strategy earned around +1 bp per roundtrip before fees but -1.9621 after fees (18927 trades). The maker versions of the same signal lost -0.4705 without a cancel rule (8851 trades) and -0.4921 with one (7333 trades), net of fees; a naive maker lost -0.4307. The authors say the maker strategies are primarily undermined by fill probability: they almost always miss out on favorable price moves and keep the fills corresponding to reversals. Latency is ignored there, potentially leading to an overstatement of results. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Queue-aware simulation needs an explicit queue-position model. hftbacktest is replay-based (no market impact) and supports Market-By-Price data; it offers RiskAverseQueueModel (the most conservative: cancellations and modifications in the book happen only at the tail of the queue, and the queue position advances only if a trade happens at the price) and ProbQueueModel (PowerProbQueueFunc and LogProbQueueFunc variants), with NoPartialFillExchange as the default exchange simulation. a vendor article adds that queue position should be seeded at ack time, not decision time, and that a maker strategy is deployable only if it survives at the conservative edge of the bracket of fill rules. (medium confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/
- [statement] On Lighter the cancel-on-cross outcome does not appear in the API reply. The docs say an API response with code: 200 means accepted, not executed, and that an order cancelled by matching rules (for example post-only would cross) is a successful transaction that consumes its nonce. A bot must confirm the order's fate on the WebSocket account channels or with GET /api/v1/tx. (medium confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/order-types-and-matching
- [statement] During a Hyperliquid network upgrade's post-only period, market orders and TWAP suborders do not fill. A Hummingbot user logged 'Only post-only orders allowed immediately after a network upgrade' after a 500 code server disconnect (opened on Dec 20, 2023). A taker-only strategy has no path in that window, while a post-only converted strategy can still place orders. This rests on one 2023 bug report plus the docs. (medium confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/order-types · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/6730
- [statement] Self-trade prevention can cancel a hybrid strategy's own orders. Paradex's create-order endpoint has an stp field (Self Trade Prevention: EXPIRE_MAKER, EXPIRE_TAKER or EXPIRE_BOTH) that defaults to EXPIRE_TAKER if empty, and Lighter lists self-trade prevention among the matching-rule cancels. A taker fallback or opposite-side order that meets the strategy's own resting quote may therefore be cancelled. (medium confidence) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/prod/orders/new · keywords: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts
